summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was readmitted five days after prior discharge for worsening right hip and bilateral SI joint pain. He reported severe pain limiting mobility and daily activities, with nausea preventing oral medication use. Initial labs showed elevated CRP and WBC, but no signs of infection. Imaging revealed no acute fracture. He received IV pain control initially, then transitioned to oral medications. A fluoroscopic-guided steroid injection into the right hip was performed, resulting in improved pain. He developed right anterior rib tenderness, but bone scan showed only degenerative changes without acute inflammation. Systemic steroids were not prescribed due to prior infectious complications and limited benefit. He was started on cyclobenzaprine and capsaicin for musculoskeletal pain. Persistent hematuria and proteinuria were noted, warranting outpatient urology follow-up. He was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with stable pain, a revised medication plan, and follow-up instructions.
